title: The original order does not survive the sort
prompt:
sortedAndOriginal(int[] data) must return a List<List<Integer>> with exactly two rows:
row 0 is data sorted ascending, row 1 is data in the order it was passed in. The caller
keeps using data after the call, so the array itself must come back untouched.

Arrays that arrive already sorted look perfect. Anything out of order comes back with
both rows agreeing when they should not. Find the bug and fix it - one line is enough.

Keep the class name Solution and the given method signature.
